claims.title: The Neolithic settlement of Choirokoitia
claims.summary: A farming community of round stone dwellings flourished at Choirokoitia, one of the best-preserved and most important prehistoric sites in the eastern Mediterranean, illuminating the early evolution of human society in the region.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cyprus: An island at the crossroads of three continents, Greek and Turkish, divided by a line drawn in green.", terralore.co/country/CYP/chronicle#ev-7000bce-the-neolithic-settlement-of-choirokoitia, claim TL:CYP:event:7000bce:the-neolithic-settlement-of-choirokoitia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Greek settlement and the city-kingdoms
claims.summary: After the collapse of Mycenaean Greece, Greek-speaking settlers established the city-kingdoms of Cyprus, among them Salamis, Kition and Paphos, making Greek the island's predominant language.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cyprus: An island at the crossroads of three continents, Greek and Turkish, divided by a line drawn in green.", terralore.co/country/CYP/chronicle#ev-1200bce-greek-settlement-and-the-city-kingdoms, claim TL:CYP:event:1200bce:greek-settlement-and-the-city-kingdoms, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The sanctuary of Aphrodite at Paphos
claims.summary: Old Paphos became the principal centre of the worship of Aphrodite, whose temple bore witness to one of the oldest Mycenaean settlements and drew pilgrims from across the Greek world.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cyprus: An island at the crossroads of three continents, Greek and Turkish, divided by a line drawn in green.", terralore.co/country/CYP/chronicle#ev-1200bce-the-sanctuary-of-aphrodite-at-paphos, claim TL:CYP:event:1200bce:the-sanctuary-of-aphrodite-at-paphos, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Assyrian, Egyptian and Persian overlordship
claims.summary: The Cypriot kingdoms paid tribute successively to the Assyrian, Egyptian and Persian empires, sharing in the wider Greek world's long struggle against Persian domination.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cyprus: An island at the crossroads of three continents, Greek and Turkish, divided by a line drawn in green.", terralore.co/country/CYP/chronicle#ev-709bce-assyrian-egyptian-and-persian-overlordship, claim TL:CYP:event:709bce:assyrian-egyptian-and-persian-overlordship, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ptolemaic rule
claims.summary: Following Alexander the Great's conquests, Cyprus passed to the Hellenistic Ptolemies of Egypt, who abolished the independent city-kingdoms and governed the island as a province until Rome took it in 58 BCE.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cyprus: An island at the crossroads of three continents, Greek and Turkish, divided by a line drawn in green.", terralore.co/country/CYP/chronicle#ev-294bce-ptolemaic-rule, claim TL:CYP:event:294bce:ptolemaic-rule, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rome annexes Cyprus
claims.summary: Cyprus was annexed by Rome and organised as a province; under Roman rule the island prospered, with Nea Paphos as its capital and a centre of the celebrated mosaic art later inscribed by UNESCO.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cyprus: An island at the crossroads of three continents, Greek and Turkish, divided by a line drawn in green.", terralore.co/country/CYP/chronicle#ev-58bce-rome-annexes-cyprus, claim TL:CYP:event:58bce:rome-annexes-cyprus, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Paul and Barnabas convert the proconsul
claims.summary: On their journey across Cyprus the apostles Paul and Barnabas reached the Roman proconsul Sergius Paulus at Paphos, an early instance of a senior Roman official embracing Christianity.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cyprus: An island at the crossroads of three continents, Greek and Turkish, divided by a line drawn in green.", terralore.co/country/CYP/chronicle#ev-45-paul-and-barnabas-convert-the-proconsul, claim TL:CYP:event:45:paul-and-barnabas-convert-the-proconsul, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: An autocephalous Church
claims.summary: The Church of Cyprus was recognised as self-governing (autocephalous), free from the authority of any neighbouring patriarch, a distinction its archbishops have defended throughout the island's history.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cyprus: An island at the crossroads of three continents, Greek and Turkish, divided by a line drawn in green.", terralore.co/country/CYP/chronicle#ev-431-an-autocephalous-church, claim TL:CYP:event:431:an-autocephalous-church, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Arab raids and a contested frontier
claims.summary: From the mid-seventh century Cyprus suffered repeated Arab naval raids and for some three centuries lay as a contested zone between Byzantium and the Caliphate before Byzantine rule was firmly restored in 965.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cyprus: An island at the crossroads of three continents, Greek and Turkish, divided by a line drawn in green.", terralore.co/country/CYP/chronicle#ev-649-arab-raids-and-a-contested-frontier, claim TL:CYP:event:649:arab-raids-and-a-contested-frontier, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The painted churches of the Troödos
claims.summary: The mountain region of Troödos accumulated one of the largest groups of Byzantine churches and monasteries, richly decorated with murals later inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List.

sources.label: Painted Churches in the Troödos Region (World Heritage List, inscribed 1985)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cyprus: An island at the crossroads of three continents, Greek and Turkish, divided by a line drawn in green.", terralore.co/country/CYP/chronicle#ev-1100-the-painted-churches-of-the-troodos, claim TL:CYP:event:1100:the-painted-churches-of-the-troodos, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Richard the Lionheart seizes Cyprus
claims.summary: En route to the Third Crusade, King Richard I of England captured Cyprus from its Byzantine governor, ending Byzantine rule and opening the island to Latin Crusader control.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cyprus: An island at the crossroads of three continents, Greek and Turkish, divided by a line drawn in green.", terralore.co/country/CYP/chronicle#ev-1191-richard-the-lionheart-seizes-cyprus, claim TL:CYP:event:1191:richard-the-lionheart-seizes-cyprus, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Lusignan Kingdom of Cyprus
claims.summary: Guy de Lusignan, former king of Jerusalem, took possession of Cyprus, founding a French feudal dynasty that ruled the island as a Latin Crusader kingdom for nearly three centuries.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cyprus: An island at the crossroads of three continents, Greek and Turkish, divided by a line drawn in green.", terralore.co/country/CYP/chronicle#ev-1192-the-lusignan-kingdom-of-cyprus, claim TL:CYP:event:1192:the-lusignan-kingdom-of-cyprus, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Cyprus ceded to Venice
claims.summary: Caterina Cornaro, widow of the last Lusignan king, ceded Cyprus to the Republic of Venice, which ruled it as a fortified colonial outpost and bulwark against the Ottomans.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cyprus: An island at the crossroads of three continents, Greek and Turkish, divided by a line drawn in green.", terralore.co/country/CYP/chronicle#ev-1489-cyprus-ceded-to-venice, claim TL:CYP:event:1489:cyprus-ceded-to-venice, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ottoman conquest of Cyprus
claims.summary: An Ottoman army invaded in 1570, taking Nicosia, and after a long siege captured Famagusta in 1571, ending Venetian rule and beginning more than three centuries of Ottoman administration.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cyprus: An island at the crossroads of three continents, Greek and Turkish, divided by a line drawn in green.", terralore.co/country/CYP/chronicle#ev-1570-ottoman-conquest-of-cyprus, claim TL:CYP:event:1570:ottoman-conquest-of-cyprus, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Two communities take shape
claims.summary: Under Ottoman rule the Orthodox Church was restored and its archbishop made leader of the Greek Cypriots, while Muslim settlement established the Turkish Cypriot community alongside it.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cyprus: An island at the crossroads of three continents, Greek and Turkish, divided by a line drawn in green.", terralore.co/country/CYP/chronicle#ev-1572-two-communities-take-shape, claim TL:CYP:event:1572:two-communities-take-shape, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Britain takes over Cyprus
claims.summary: Under the Cyprus Convention, Britain assumed the administration of Cyprus from the Ottoman Empire, which retained nominal sovereignty, gaining a strategic Mediterranean base near the route to India.

sources.label: A Guide to the History of Recognition, Diplomatic and Consular Relations: Cyprus
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cyprus: An island at the crossroads of three continents, Greek and Turkish, divided by a line drawn in green.", terralore.co/country/CYP/chronicle#ev-1878-britain-takes-over-cyprus, claim TL:CYP:event:1878:britain-takes-over-cyprus, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: British annexation
claims.summary: When the Ottoman Empire joined the First World War against Britain, Britain annexed Cyprus; Turkey renounced its claim to the island in the 1923 Treaty of Lausanne.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cyprus: An island at the crossroads of three continents, Greek and Turkish, divided by a line drawn in green.", terralore.co/country/CYP/chronicle#ev-1914-british-annexation, claim TL:CYP:event:1914:british-annexation, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Cyprus made a Crown Colony
claims.summary: Cyprus was formally declared a British Crown Colony, consolidating colonial administration over the island.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cyprus: An island at the crossroads of three continents, Greek and Turkish, divided by a line drawn in green.", terralore.co/country/CYP/chronicle#ev-1925-cyprus-made-a-crown-colony, claim TL:CYP:event:1925:cyprus-made-a-crown-colony, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The énosis plebiscite
claims.summary: The Orthodox Church organised a plebiscite in which the overwhelming majority of Greek Cypriots voted for union with Greece; Britain refused, and Turkish Cypriots opposed it, sharpening communal division.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cyprus: An island at the crossroads of three continents, Greek and Turkish, divided by a line drawn in green.", terralore.co/country/CYP/chronicle#ev-1950-the-enosis-plebiscite, claim TL:CYP:event:1950:the-enosis-plebiscite, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: EOKA launches its armed campaign
claims.summary: EOKA, led by Colonel Georgios Grivas with the support of Archbishop Makarios III, began an armed struggle against British rule in pursuit of énosis, opening four years of insurgency and repression.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cyprus: An island at the crossroads of three continents, Greek and Turkish, divided by a line drawn in green.", terralore.co/country/CYP/chronicle#ev-1955-eoka-launches-its-armed-campaign, claim TL:CYP:event:1955:eoka-launches-its-armed-campaign, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Zürich-London Agreements
claims.summary: Greece and Turkey reached a compromise at Zürich, endorsed in London by Britain and Cypriot leaders, setting the terms for an independent Cyprus that excluded both énosis and partition.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cyprus: An island at the crossroads of three continents, Greek and Turkish, divided by a line drawn in green.", terralore.co/country/CYP/chronicle#ev-1959-the-zurich-london-agreements, claim TL:CYP:event:1959:the-zurich-london-agreements, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence and the Treaty of Guarantee
claims.summary: The Republic of Cyprus became independent under a Greek-Turkish power-sharing constitution; the Treaty of Guarantee bound Britain, Greece and Turkey to its independence and territorial integrity, and Britain kept two Sovereign Base Areas.

sources.label: Treaty of Guarantee, signed at Nicosia, 16 August 1960
A Guide to the History of Recognition, Diplomatic and Consular Relations: Cyprus
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: Breakdown and the Green Line
claims.summary: After President Makarios proposed constitutional changes, intercommunal violence broke out in December 1963; Turkish Cypriots withdrew from government and a ceasefire line dubbed the 'Green Line' was drawn through Nicosia.

sources.label: Establishment of UNFICYP (Security Council Resolution 186, 4 March 1964)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cyprus: An island at the crossroads of three continents, Greek and Turkish, divided by a line drawn in green.", terralore.co/country/CYP/chronicle#ev-1963-breakdown-and-the-green-line, claim TL:CYP:event:1963:breakdown-and-the-green-line, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: UN Security Council Resolution 186 establishes UNFICYP
claims.summary: The Security Council unanimously recommended, with the consent of the Government of Cyprus, the creation of the UN Peace-keeping Force in Cyprus to prevent a recurrence of fighting and help restore order; UNFICYP became operational on 27 March 1964.

sources.label: Establishment of UNFICYP (Security Council Resolution 186, 4 March 1964)
UNFICYP: United Nations Peacekeeping Force in Cyprus
UNFICYP – United Nations Force in Cyprus
sources.publisher: Permanent Mission of the Republic of Cyprus to the United Nations

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cyprus: An island at the crossroads of three continents, Greek and Turkish, divided by a line drawn in green.", terralore.co/country/CYP/chronicle#ev-1964-un-security-council-resolution-186-establishes, claim TL:CYP:event:1964:un-security-council-resolution-186-establishes, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: A UN mediator for the Cyprus question
claims.summary: Resolution 186 also recommended that the Secretary-General designate a mediator to promote a peaceful and agreed settlement, beginning the long international effort to resolve the dispute.

sources.label: Establishment of UNFICYP (Security Council Resolution 186, 4 March 1964)
UNFICYP – United Nations Force in Cyprus
sources.publisher: Permanent Mission of the Republic of Cyprus to the United Nations

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cyprus: An island at the crossroads of three continents, Greek and Turkish, divided by a line drawn in green.", terralore.co/country/CYP/chronicle#ev-1964-a-un-mediator-for-the-cyprus-question, claim TL:CYP:event:1964:a-un-mediator-for-the-cyprus-question, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Greek-junta-backed coup
claims.summary: The military junta ruling Greece, through the Cypriot National Guard, overthrew President Makarios in pursuit of énosis; Makarios escaped abroad and a hardline nationalist was installed.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cyprus: An island at the crossroads of three continents, Greek and Turkish, divided by a line drawn in green.", terralore.co/country/CYP/chronicle#ev-1974-the-greek-junta-backed-coup, claim TL:CYP:event:1974:the-greek-junta-backed-coup, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Turkish military intervention
claims.summary: Invoking its guarantor rights under the 1960 Treaty of Guarantee, Turkey landed forces on 20 July 1974 and in a second August offensive took the northern third of the island, partitioning Cyprus and displacing both communities; UNFICYP was thereafter tasked with supervising the ceasefire lines and the buffer zone.

sources.label: Treaty of Guarantee, signed at Nicosia, 16 August 1960
UNFICYP: United Nations Peacekeeping Force in Cyprus

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cyprus: An island at the crossroads of three continents, Greek and Turkish, divided by a line drawn in green.", terralore.co/country/CYP/chronicle#ev-1974-turkish-military-intervention, claim TL:CYP:event:1974:turkish-military-intervention, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Declaration of the 'TRNC' and UN Resolution 541
claims.summary: The Turkish Cypriot leadership proclaimed the 'Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus' on 15 November 1983; on 18 November the Security Council, in Resolution 541, considered the declaration legally invalid and called on all states not to recognise any Cypriot state other than the Republic of Cyprus.

sources.label: UNFICYP: United Nations Peacekeeping Force in Cyprus

sources.publisher: Permanent Mission of the Republic of Cyprus to the United Nations

claims.title: The Annan Plan referendums
claims.summary: A UN reunification plan was put to simultaneous referendums; Turkish Cypriots approved it but about three-quarters of Greek Cypriots voting rejected it, leaving the island divided on the eve of EU membership.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cyprus: An island at the crossroads of three continents, Greek and Turkish, divided by a line drawn in green.", terralore.co/country/CYP/chronicle#ev-2004-the-annan-plan-referendums, claim TL:CYP:event:2004:the-annan-plan-referendums, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Accession to the European Union
claims.summary: The Republic of Cyprus joined the EU; the whole island is EU territory, but the application of EU law is suspended in the northern areas not under the government's effective control.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cyprus: An island at the crossroads of three continents, Greek and Turkish, divided by a line drawn in green.", terralore.co/country/CYP/chronicle#ev-2004-accession-to-the-european-union, claim TL:CYP:event:2004:accession-to-the-european-union, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
